name: Mastodon Public API (mastodon.social)
summary: Keyless read endpoints for trends, hashtag timelines, directory and search on a Mastodon server, tested on mastodon.social.
description: Every Mastodon server exposes the same REST API under /api/v1 and /api/v2. On mastodon.social, trending hashtags and links, hashtag timelines, the profile directory, hashtag search and server info work without a token. Each server decides which endpoints are public: the global public timeline on mastodon.social now demands authentication. Because Mastodon is federated, the base URL can be swapped for any other instance, whose settings may differ.

auth.notes: Trends, hashtag timelines, directory, hashtag search and instance info worked without a token on mastodon.social. Posting, home timelines and the public timeline need an OAuth token there.

rate_limit.summary: Documented: all endpoints can be called 300 times within 5 minutes per IP. The x-ratelimit-limit header showed 300 on the example.

endpoints.summary: Search; type=hashtags worked without a token

license.name: Not stated; posts are user-generated content, per-instance terms apply

coverage.temporal: Recent posts and trends on the queried server

agent_notes: Follow the next link in the Link response header (max_id based) to page timelines. Counts in history entries are strings and day is a Unix timestamp. To query another instance, change the host and retest, since admins can restrict endpoints. The tag timeline includes posts federated from other servers.
caveats: GET /v1/timelines/public returned 422 'This method requires an authenticated user' on mastodon.social.
Behaviour differs per server (auth requirements, limits, enabled trends); this record only covers what was seen on mastodon.social.

verification.notes: Exact example executed without credentials on mastodon.social; tag timeline, trends/links, v2 search, directory and instance also returned 200.
